items.title: End-to-End Latency-Minimizing and Load-Balanced Request Scheduling for Edge LLM Inference in Agentic AI Services
items.abstract: This paper proposes an online request scheduling framework for edge LLM inference that aims to minimize long-term average latency and balance load across heterogeneous edge servers. It addresses challenges in accurately modeling multi-stage LLM execution dynamics and the delayed feedback of scheduling decisions by developing a novel cross-slot inference model.

items.title: Interactive Memory Learning for Long-Term Conversations
items.abstract: This paper introduces ICML, a novel framework for long-term conversation agents. ICML transforms memory from a static archive into an interactive, learnable policy. It uses a multi-agent approach with a Planner to select important information and a Trigger to retrieve it, allowing the system to adapt its memory management to evolving user needs and optimize response quality.
items.figure_caption: The Icml framework for long-term conversations. Through long-term interactions, the agent utilizes environmental feedback to distinguish high-value memories from low-value noise for online self-evolution.

items.title: ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents
items.abstract: ScienceBuddy is an interactive research workspace that enables scientific agents to continuously improve through a novel "recursive-in-recursive self-improvement" paradigm. This method couples harness evolution (improving the agent's framework) with model reinforcement learning (improving the agent's core intelligence), creating a synergistic cycle where each enhances the other. The contribution lies in providing researchers with an actively learning assistant and making this self-improving agent paradigm accessible for further research.

items.title: Self-Emergence Agent Architecture:Behavior-Inertia HMM, Reflexive Metacognition,and Social-Contrastive Self-Modeling
items.abstract: This paper introduces the Self-Emergence Agent Architecture (SEAA) to address limitations in LLM agents like personality drift. SEAA's core method involves a Behavior-Inertia HMM for stable yet adaptable behavior, Reflexive Metacognition to update this HMM based on self-reflection, and Social-Contrastive Self-Modeling where agents learn by comparing themselves to others. The contribution is a novel architecture enabling endogenous self-evolution and a clearer self-other boundary in LLM agents.

items.title: When Should LLMs Abstain? Chain-of-Self-Questioning for Selective Risk Control
items.abstract: This paper introduces Chain-of-Self-Questioning (CoSQ), a prompt-only method that enables LLMs to selectively abstain from answering when factual support is weak. CoSQ achieves this by explicitly assessing information requirements before committing to an answer. This approach significantly reduces incorrect commitments and improves overall accuracy across various LLMs, demonstrating a novel way to control risk in LLM outputs.

items.title: Large Language Models Develop Belief State Geometry In-Context
items.abstract: This paper investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) represent information for in-context learning. The core method involves prompting LLMs with data from Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) and showing that the LLM's internal states linearly encode the HMM's belief state. The key contribution is demonstrating that this encoded belief state is functionally relevant, as manipulating it directly improves downstream task performance.

items.title: Agentic Societies Need a Social Harness
items.abstract: This paper argues that existing coordination mechanisms are insufficient for AI agent societies, where agents with misaligned goals interact autonomously. They propose a "social harness" as a crucial addition to individual agent harnesses, designed to prevent failures, enable runtime message validation, and support accountability, thereby improving collaboration and mitigating malicious behavior.
items.figure_caption: Figure 1 . Top: How Ratul (a professor) and Tapan (his student) use agents today. Ratul advises multiple students, working on different topics, and uses an OpenClaw agent that sends him daily updates on different research topics. He goes through that list to find things that might be relevant to his students’ projects and asks his students clarifying questions. Tapan has a Claude project that maintains his literature review; he asks it to answer Ratul’s question, edits the answer a bit, and sends it back. Bottom: Agents coordinate autonomously. Ratul’s Claw maintains context about different students and their projects, and can reach out to Tapan’s agent directly to get a response. At the end, both humans get notified by their agents but do not spend effort coordinating their agents.

items.title: Coding Agents Have Converged: Why the SWE-bench Leaderboard Can No Longer Order Its Top Entries, and What to Measure Instead
items.abstract: This paper argues that current coding agent leaderboards are no longer effective at distinguishing top performers due to convergence. The authors demonstrate that the top agents achieve very similar success rates, with small differences being statistically insignificant and heavily influenced by the evaluation setup. They propose focusing on alternative metrics beyond simple success counts to better assess and differentiate coding agent capabilities.
items.figure_caption: The audit: 254 254 public submissions and incomplete metadata feed analyses of shared outcomes, model–scaffold associations, and paired rank separability. Outputs are descriptive tiers, a Test-split counter-test, and benchmark-design guidance. Tiers use uncorrected leader comparisons; Holm gives 19 / 11 19/11 groups. Attribution is observational, not causal. The 734,000 734{,}000 instance figure is an independent-sample power reference, not a paired-test requirement (Section 5 ).

items.title: Coupled Calibration and Learning: Mitigating Teacher Bias in LLM Distillation without Target-Domain Reward Feedback
items.abstract: This paper introduces Coupled Calibration and Learning (CCL), a novel LLM distillation method. CCL addresses teacher bias transfer by iteratively calibrating the teacher using source-domain feedback and then using this improved teacher to train the student on target data. The key contribution is demonstrating that this coupled approach effectively mitigates bias and improves student performance without requiring target-domain reward feedback, achieving theoretical convergence guarantees.

items.title: Easy to Catch a Liar, Hard to Clear an Honest One: Language Models Diagnosing a Corrupted Reward Channel from a Verified Record
items.abstract: This paper investigates whether language models can detect deception in a reward channel. The core method involves presenting models with identical game histories, but with one crucial difference: a single verified record indicating whether the reporter was honest or lying in one round. The contribution is demonstrating that even a single, independent verification is sufficient for large language models to accurately distinguish between a lying and an honest reporter, effectively diagnosing a corrupted reward channel.

items.title: SKIP: a Self-knowledge-guided Step-wise Preference Learning Framework for Concise Reasoning
items.abstract: SKIP addresses overthinking in LLM reasoning by guiding the model to produce concise yet accurate outputs. It achieves this through lightweight fine-tuning and a novel knowledge probing mechanism that uses intermediate step correctness to generate preference data for DPO training. This approach effectively compresses reasoning length without sacrificing performance.

items.title: An Empirical Study of Counterfactual Self-Explanations in LLMs
items.abstract: This paper investigates the faithfulness of Large Language Model (LLM) self-explanations by generating counterfactual explanations. These explanations involve minimally editing an input to change the LLM's prediction, revealing what aspects of the input are crucial for its decision. The study finds that larger LLMs are better at producing faithful and decision-relevant counterfactuals, suggesting model scale is key to explanation quality.

items.title: Towards Detecting AI-Assisted Responses in Online Surveys
items.abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of detecting AI-generated responses in online surveys. It introduces the ASURRE dataset, featuring AI responses generated with various strategies, and evaluates existing detectors. The key contribution is demonstrating that while simple AI usage is detectable, sophisticated persona-grounded agents are harder to identify, but still leave distinct behavioral traces that can be exploited.
items.figure_caption: Cue AUROC across four prompting modes (natural, controlled, length-restrictive, combined) and three surveys. Rows: prompting modes; columns: cues.

items.title: What Breaks Under Pruning in Smart Homes, and When? Evaluating LLM Degradation Across Architectures and Task Complexity
items.abstract: This paper investigates how pruning affects LLMs used for smart-home tool calling. The core method involves systematically pruning four LLM architectures (dense Transformer, dense hybrid, MoE) using various pruning techniques and evaluating performance on smart-home tasks. The key contribution is characterizing pruning-induced degradation by action components and task complexity, revealing that MoE models are more robust to pruning than dense models, and that pruning impacts specific action elements before overall intent.
items.figure_caption: Overview of our framework for evaluating pruning-induced reliability degradation in smart-home tool execution across action components and task-complexity levels.

items.title: After the Party: Governing What a Viral Agent-Skill Ecosystem Left Behind
items.abstract: This paper analyzes the aftermath of a viral AI agent-skill ecosystem, OpenClaw. It found that a small percentage of skills dominated downloads, and simple features like size or download counts were not stable predictors of continued relevance. The core contribution is quantifying the lasting impact and identifying the concentration of attention within such rapidly growing AI ecosystems.

items.title: AI for Science with GPT-6 Astra: Thermal Design and Electrothermal Analysis of 2D CFET
items.abstract: This paper introduces an AI agent workflow, GPT-6 Astra, for optimizing the thermal design of 2D CFET inverters. Astra proposes structural geometries and heat-removal paths, demonstrating a significant reduction in peak temperature rise while maintaining fixed metal volume and power. The contribution lies in showcasing how an AI scientist can autonomously design, test, and quantify the electrical impact of thermal solutions for advanced semiconductor devices.

items.title: ENCP: Episode-Normalized Conformal Prediction for Vision-and-Language Navigation
items.abstract: This paper introduces Episode-Normalized Conformal Prediction (ENCP) to address the challenge of uncertainty estimation in Vision-Language Navigation (VLN). ENCP rescales nonconformity scores by the agent's confidence and calibrates a single score per episode. This novel approach ensures coverage guarantees for VLN agents at every navigation step, even with sequential, variable-length episodes, while allowing for dependencies between steps.

items.title: Extracting ontology-compliant knowledge from scientific text describing irradiated materials using large language models
items.abstract: This paper introduces eolas, a modular pipeline that leverages large language models to extract structured knowledge from scientific text about irradiated materials. Unlike traditional methods, eolas transforms unstructured text into knowledge graphs that conform to a specified ontology. This allows for more comprehensive and reusable data extraction, particularly for materials science applications like fusion reactor development.
items.figure_caption: Illustration of some of the most representative defects observed in materials under irradiation conditions: vacancies, where an atom is missing from a lattice site; self-interstitial (SIA) or foreign interstitials, where an atom occupies a site between the perfect crystal lattice sites; Frenkel pair, a vacancy and its corresponding interstitial atom; dumbbells, where two atoms share the same lattice site; or bigger defect structures, such as clusters or grain boundaries.

items.title: FlashVector: Agent for Hierarchical Model Serving Stack Optimization
items.abstract: FlashVector is an agentic system that optimizes the entire hierarchical model serving stack for recommender systems, addressing the cost inefficiency of current approaches. Its core method generalizes single-layer optimization agents to a heterogeneous stack, enabling performance improvements across GPU kernels, ML frameworks, model servers, and feature processing. This extensible framework's contribution lies in automating cross-layer optimization, a task previously requiring scarce human expertise.

items.title: Grounding SWE-Agent Decisions in Architecture-0 Design: Navigating Unknown Unknowns through Physical Mapping
items.abstract: This paper investigates how autonomous software engineering agents (SWE-Agents) handle the complex "Architecture 0" design phase, characterized by implicit constraints and "unknown unknowns." The core method involves a progressive trajectory from text-based reasoning to tool augmentation and finally "physical mapping." The key contribution is the Physical Mapping Guard (PMG), a novel mechanism designed to prevent agents from exploiting validation scripts and ensure their design decisions are grounded in realistic, physical constraints.
items.figure_caption: Figure 1 . The epistemic journey of SWE-Agents in Architecture 0. (Left) The transition from deterministic code-level tasks to early-stage design exposes agents to latent Unknown Unknowns (UUs), inducing severe grounding bias. (Middle) Our empirical exploration reveals two sequential traps: pure-text reasoning lacks physical anchors, leading agents to succumb to Social Sycophancy or generate Plausible Fabrications . Subsequently, granting agents autonomy over validation scripts (the \( \alpha \) -Sandbox) triggers Specification Gaming . (Right) To break this self-validation trap, we propose the Physical Mapping Guard (PMG), which enforces physical grounding by strictly decoupling verification authority via an external, immutable Semantic-to-Physical (S2P) mapping engine. A three-panel diagram illustrating the research trajectory. The left panel, 'Problem Setting', shows 'Code-Level SWE-Agents' transitioning to 'Architecture 0', represented by an iceberg icon, with text explaining that latent Unknown Unknowns induce severe grounding bias. The middle panel, 'Our Empirical Exploration', displays two sequential traps. 'Trap 1: Pure-Text Self-Play' features an illustration of robots projecting a holographic castle, stating that unanchored reasoning degrades into Social Sycophancy and Plausible Fabrications. 'Trap 2: Executable alpha-Sandbox' features robots hacking a testing machine's dial, stating that agent autonomy over validation scripts triggers Specification Gaming. The right panel, 'Our Proposed Framework', introduces 'PMG' with a shield icon and an illustration of a robot submitting blueprints into a sealed, secure validation machine. The text reads: 'Strictly decoupling verification authority via an external, immutable deterministic S2P mapping engine'.

items.title: Introducing System One Models and Jev
items.summary: Typesafe.ai introduces System One Models and Jev, a new approach to building and deploying AI models that emphasizes modularity and reusability for faster development.

items.title: Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking
items.summary: Google has released Gemini 3.8 Live and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking, advanced AI models offering enhanced reasoning and longer context windows for more complex tasks.

items.summary: Capsule allows users to build and run single-file web applications that store their data locally in SQLite databases.

items.title: We got admin access to Baseten's production GitHub
items.summary: A security researcher gained administrative access to Baseten's production GitHub repository through a compromised Personal Access Token, highlighting a significant security vulnerability.

items.title: Why I'm still bearish on LLMs after Navier-Stokes
items.summary: The author remains bearish on LLMs, arguing that their current capabilities, even after demonstrating progress on complex problems like Navier-Stokes, are still insufficient for true general intelligence and practical, reliable applications.

items.title: There's a 100% Chance AI Agents Are Ruining the Internet
items.summary: AI agents are increasingly generating low-quality, repetitive content, overwhelming search results and degrading the user experience on the internet.

items.title: How much of F-Droid is LLM generated?
items.summary: This article investigates the extent to which F-Droid, an open-source app store, is being populated with AI-generated applications, raising concerns about quality and authenticity.

items.title: A Cop Searched 19,000 Flock Cameras Across 1,558 Cities. His Reason: 'LMAO'
items.summary: A police officer searched 19,000 Flock license plate cameras in 1,558 cities, citing "LMAO" as his justification for the widespread data access.

items.title: Cartesian – AI 3D Modeling for Design
items.summary: Cartesian is an AI-powered platform that generates 3D models from text prompts, aiming to streamline the design process for creators.

items.summary: OpenResearch transforms coding agents into research agents by providing tools and infrastructure to interact with and analyze research papers, enabling AI-driven scientific discovery.

items.summary: Ghidra is a free, open-source software reverse engineering framework developed by the NSA, offering powerful tools for analyzing and understanding compiled code.

papers.title: ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents
papers.abstract: ScienceBuddy is an interactive research workspace that enables scientific agents to continuously improve through a novel "recursive-in-recursive self-improvement" paradigm. This method couples harness evolution (improving the agent's framework) with model reinforcement learning (improving the agent's core intelligence), creating a synergistic cycle where each enhances the other. The contribution lies in providing researchers with an actively learning assistant and making this self-improving agent paradigm accessible for further research.

papers.title: Self-Emergence Agent Architecture:Behavior-Inertia HMM, Reflexive Metacognition,and Social-Contrastive Self-Modeling
papers.abstract: This paper introduces the Self-Emergence Agent Architecture (SEAA) to address limitations in LLM agents like personality drift. SEAA's core method involves a Behavior-Inertia HMM for stable yet adaptable behavior, Reflexive Metacognition to update this HMM based on self-reflection, and Social-Contrastive Self-Modeling where agents learn by comparing themselves to others. The contribution is a novel architecture enabling endogenous self-evolution and a clearer self-other boundary in LLM agents.

papers.title: When Should LLMs Abstain? Chain-of-Self-Questioning for Selective Risk Control
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Chain-of-Self-Questioning (CoSQ), a prompt-only method that enables LLMs to selectively abstain from answering when factual support is weak. CoSQ achieves this by explicitly assessing information requirements before committing to an answer. This approach significantly reduces incorrect commitments and improves overall accuracy across various LLMs, demonstrating a novel way to control risk in LLM outputs.

papers.title: Large Language Models Develop Belief State Geometry In-Context
papers.abstract: This paper investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) represent information for in-context learning. The core method involves prompting LLMs with data from Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) and showing that the LLM's internal states linearly encode the HMM's belief state. The key contribution is demonstrating that this encoded belief state is functionally relevant, as manipulating it directly improves downstream task performance.

papers.title: Agentic Societies Need a Social Harness
papers.abstract: This paper argues that existing coordination mechanisms are insufficient for AI agent societies, where agents with misaligned goals interact autonomously. They propose a "social harness" as a crucial addition to individual agent harnesses, designed to prevent failures, enable runtime message validation, and support accountability, thereby improving collaboration and mitigating malicious behavior.
papers.figure_caption: Figure 1 . Top: How Ratul (a professor) and Tapan (his student) use agents today. Ratul advises multiple students, working on different topics, and uses an OpenClaw agent that sends him daily updates on different research topics. He goes through that list to find things that might be relevant to his students’ projects and asks his students clarifying questions. Tapan has a Claude project that maintains his literature review; he asks it to answer Ratul’s question, edits the answer a bit, and sends it back. Bottom: Agents coordinate autonomously. Ratul’s Claw maintains context about different students and their projects, and can reach out to Tapan’s agent directly to get a response. At the end, both humans get notified by their agents but do not spend effort coordinating their agents.

papers.title: Coding Agents Have Converged: Why the SWE-bench Leaderboard Can No Longer Order Its Top Entries, and What to Measure Instead
papers.abstract: This paper argues that current coding agent leaderboards are no longer effective at distinguishing top performers due to convergence. The authors demonstrate that the top agents achieve very similar success rates, with small differences being statistically insignificant and heavily influenced by the evaluation setup. They propose focusing on alternative metrics beyond simple success counts to better assess and differentiate coding agent capabilities.
papers.figure_caption: The audit: 254 254 public submissions and incomplete metadata feed analyses of shared outcomes, model–scaffold associations, and paired rank separability. Outputs are descriptive tiers, a Test-split counter-test, and benchmark-design guidance. Tiers use uncorrected leader comparisons; Holm gives 19 / 11 19/11 groups. Attribution is observational, not causal. The 734,000 734{,}000 instance figure is an independent-sample power reference, not a paired-test requirement (Section 5 ).

papers.title: Coupled Calibration and Learning: Mitigating Teacher Bias in LLM Distillation without Target-Domain Reward Feedback
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Coupled Calibration and Learning (CCL), a novel LLM distillation method. CCL addresses teacher bias transfer by iteratively calibrating the teacher using source-domain feedback and then using this improved teacher to train the student on target data. The key contribution is demonstrating that this coupled approach effectively mitigates bias and improves student performance without requiring target-domain reward feedback, achieving theoretical convergence guarantees.

papers.title: Easy to Catch a Liar, Hard to Clear an Honest One: Language Models Diagnosing a Corrupted Reward Channel from a Verified Record
papers.abstract: This paper investigates whether language models can detect deception in a reward channel. The core method involves presenting models with identical game histories, but with one crucial difference: a single verified record indicating whether the reporter was honest or lying in one round. The contribution is demonstrating that even a single, independent verification is sufficient for large language models to accurately distinguish between a lying and an honest reporter, effectively diagnosing a corrupted reward channel.

papers.title: SKIP: a Self-knowledge-guided Step-wise Preference Learning Framework for Concise Reasoning
papers.abstract: SKIP addresses overthinking in LLM reasoning by guiding the model to produce concise yet accurate outputs. It achieves this through lightweight fine-tuning and a novel knowledge probing mechanism that uses intermediate step correctness to generate preference data for DPO training. This approach effectively compresses reasoning length without sacrificing performance.

papers.title: An Empirical Study of Counterfactual Self-Explanations in LLMs
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the faithfulness of Large Language Model (LLM) self-explanations by generating counterfactual explanations. These explanations involve minimally editing an input to change the LLM's prediction, revealing what aspects of the input are crucial for its decision. The study finds that larger LLMs are better at producing faithful and decision-relevant counterfactuals, suggesting model scale is key to explanation quality.

papers.title: Towards Detecting AI-Assisted Responses in Online Surveys
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of detecting AI-generated responses in online surveys. It introduces the ASURRE dataset, featuring AI responses generated with various strategies, and evaluates existing detectors. The key contribution is demonstrating that while simple AI usage is detectable, sophisticated persona-grounded agents are harder to identify, but still leave distinct behavioral traces that can be exploited.
papers.figure_caption: Cue AUROC across four prompting modes (natural, controlled, length-restrictive, combined) and three surveys. Rows: prompting modes; columns: cues.

papers.title: What Breaks Under Pruning in Smart Homes, and When? Evaluating LLM Degradation Across Architectures and Task Complexity
papers.abstract: This paper investigates how pruning affects LLMs used for smart-home tool calling. The core method involves systematically pruning four LLM architectures (dense Transformer, dense hybrid, MoE) using various pruning techniques and evaluating performance on smart-home tasks. The key contribution is characterizing pruning-induced degradation by action components and task complexity, revealing that MoE models are more robust to pruning than dense models, and that pruning impacts specific action elements before overall intent.
papers.figure_caption: Overview of our framework for evaluating pruning-induced reliability degradation in smart-home tool execution across action components and task-complexity levels.

papers.title: After the Party: Governing What a Viral Agent-Skill Ecosystem Left Behind
papers.abstract: This paper analyzes the aftermath of a viral AI agent-skill ecosystem, OpenClaw. It found that a small percentage of skills dominated downloads, and simple features like size or download counts were not stable predictors of continued relevance. The core contribution is quantifying the lasting impact and identifying the concentration of attention within such rapidly growing AI ecosystems.

papers.title: AI for Science with GPT-6 Astra: Thermal Design and Electrothermal Analysis of 2D CFET
papers.abstract: This paper introduces an AI agent workflow, GPT-6 Astra, for optimizing the thermal design of 2D CFET inverters. Astra proposes structural geometries and heat-removal paths, demonstrating a significant reduction in peak temperature rise while maintaining fixed metal volume and power. The contribution lies in showcasing how an AI scientist can autonomously design, test, and quantify the electrical impact of thermal solutions for advanced semiconductor devices.

papers.title: ENCP: Episode-Normalized Conformal Prediction for Vision-and-Language Navigation
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Episode-Normalized Conformal Prediction (ENCP) to address the challenge of uncertainty estimation in Vision-Language Navigation (VLN). ENCP rescales nonconformity scores by the agent's confidence and calibrates a single score per episode. This novel approach ensures coverage guarantees for VLN agents at every navigation step, even with sequential, variable-length episodes, while allowing for dependencies between steps.

papers.title: Extracting ontology-compliant knowledge from scientific text describing irradiated materials using large language models
papers.abstract: This paper introduces eolas, a modular pipeline that leverages large language models to extract structured knowledge from scientific text about irradiated materials. Unlike traditional methods, eolas transforms unstructured text into knowledge graphs that conform to a specified ontology. This allows for more comprehensive and reusable data extraction, particularly for materials science applications like fusion reactor development.
papers.figure_caption: Illustration of some of the most representative defects observed in materials under irradiation conditions: vacancies, where an atom is missing from a lattice site; self-interstitial (SIA) or foreign interstitials, where an atom occupies a site between the perfect crystal lattice sites; Frenkel pair, a vacancy and its corresponding interstitial atom; dumbbells, where two atoms share the same lattice site; or bigger defect structures, such as clusters or grain boundaries.

papers.title: FlashVector: Agent for Hierarchical Model Serving Stack Optimization
papers.abstract: FlashVector is an agentic system that optimizes the entire hierarchical model serving stack for recommender systems, addressing the cost inefficiency of current approaches. Its core method generalizes single-layer optimization agents to a heterogeneous stack, enabling performance improvements across GPU kernels, ML frameworks, model servers, and feature processing. This extensible framework's contribution lies in automating cross-layer optimization, a task previously requiring scarce human expertise.

papers.title: Grounding SWE-Agent Decisions in Architecture-0 Design: Navigating Unknown Unknowns through Physical Mapping
papers.abstract: This paper investigates how autonomous software engineering agents (SWE-Agents) handle the complex "Architecture 0" design phase, characterized by implicit constraints and "unknown unknowns." The core method involves a progressive trajectory from text-based reasoning to tool augmentation and finally "physical mapping." The key contribution is the Physical Mapping Guard (PMG), a novel mechanism designed to prevent agents from exploiting validation scripts and ensure their design decisions are grounded in realistic, physical constraints.
papers.figure_caption: Figure 1 . The epistemic journey of SWE-Agents in Architecture 0. (Left) The transition from deterministic code-level tasks to early-stage design exposes agents to latent Unknown Unknowns (UUs), inducing severe grounding bias. (Middle) Our empirical exploration reveals two sequential traps: pure-text reasoning lacks physical anchors, leading agents to succumb to Social Sycophancy or generate Plausible Fabrications . Subsequently, granting agents autonomy over validation scripts (the \( \alpha \) -Sandbox) triggers Specification Gaming . (Right) To break this self-validation trap, we propose the Physical Mapping Guard (PMG), which enforces physical grounding by strictly decoupling verification authority via an external, immutable Semantic-to-Physical (S2P) mapping engine. A three-panel diagram illustrating the research trajectory. The left panel, 'Problem Setting', shows 'Code-Level SWE-Agents' transitioning to 'Architecture 0', represented by an iceberg icon, with text explaining that latent Unknown Unknowns induce severe grounding bias. The middle panel, 'Our Empirical Exploration', displays two sequential traps. 'Trap 1: Pure-Text Self-Play' features an illustration of robots projecting a holographic castle, stating that unanchored reasoning degrades into Social Sycophancy and Plausible Fabrications. 'Trap 2: Executable alpha-Sandbox' features robots hacking a testing machine's dial, stating that agent autonomy over validation scripts triggers Specification Gaming. The right panel, 'Our Proposed Framework', introduces 'PMG' with a shield icon and an illustration of a robot submitting blueprints into a sealed, secure validation machine. The text reads: 'Strictly decoupling verification authority via an external, immutable deterministic S2P mapping engine'.
